title: URL Shortener: Complete Architecture
description: Design a scalable URL shortener like bit.ly with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a URL shortening service similar to bit.ly or tinyurl.com. Users paste long URLs and receive short, shareable links. The system must handle billions of redirects per month while maintaining sub-50ms response times. Consider custom aliases, analytics, expiration policies, and high availability across geographic regions.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Shorten long URLs to 6-8 character Base62 encoded short links
Support custom aliases (e.g., /my-brand) with availability validation
Redirect short URLs to original long URLs with HTTP 301/302 status
Track analytics: click count, referrer, geographic location, device type, timestamp
Set expiration dates (TTL) or make links permanent
Generate QR codes for short URLs
Bulk create short links via CSV upload for enterprise users
Preview destination page before redirect with safety warnings

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Sub-50ms P99 redirect latency from edge cache
99.99% availability for redirect endpoints
10 million+ URLs shortened per day with horizontal scaling
Geo-distributed redirects served from nearest edge location
Immutable append-only analytics logs with 7-year retention
Rate limiting per user/IP to prevent abuse
At-least-once delivery for analytics events
Disaster recovery with cross-region database replication

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core API where shortening, redirect, analytics, and user management share a single database. This validates the Base62 encoding algorithm, collision detection, and basic redirect flow before introducing distributed complexity.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - Minimal API with clean architecture
  - Entity Framework Core for data access
  - Azure SQL Database for relational data (users, urls table)
  - Base62 encoding with collision retry logic
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service for hosting
  - Azure Blob Storage for QR code assets
  - Azure Monitor for logging
  - Single database with tables: Users, ShortUrls, Analytics, CustomAliases

data.text: At scale, split into focused microservices. The Encoding Service handles creation, the Redirect Service handles lookups with cache-first strategy, the Analytics Service processes click events asynchronously, and the User Service manages accounts and rate limits.

items: URL Encoding Service: Generates unique short codes via Base62, validates custom alias availability, prevents collisions using distributed ID generators, and persists URL mappings.
Redirect Service: Reads short codes with cache-first strategy (Redis then database), returns 301/302 redirects, logs click events to queue, and handles expired/inactive links.
Analytics Service: Consumes click events from queue, aggregates metrics (clicks, browsers, countries, devices), exposes real-time dashboards, and exports to data warehouse.
User Service: Manages accounts, API keys, rate limits per tier, bulk upload history, and billing integration for enterprise plans.
QR Code Service: Generates SVG/PNG QR codes on demand, caches generated codes, and supports custom branding colors and logos.

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: URL shorteners are read-heavy (100:1 read-to-write ratio) - cache aggressively
Use Base62 encoding with collision detection and distributed ID generation
Separate redirect path (sync, cached) from analytics (async, queued)
Custom aliases require pre-validation to prevent abuse
Edge CDN or Lambda@Edge is critical for sub-50ms global redirects
data.takeaway: A URL shortener is a cache-heavy distributed system. Optimize the redirect hot path with edge caching, offload analytics to async queues, and use Base62 with collision-safe ID generation for scale.
